key_findings: Source grounding with inline citations demonstrated (NotebookLM)
RCT evidence for learning effectiveness: LearnLM +14 percentile points, Tutor CoPilot +4 to +9 p.p.
Pedagogical action selection requires explicit control (ChatGPT) or expensive cognitive models (Cognitive Tutors)
Socratic questioning is opt-in, not universal default
Bayesian Knowledge Tracing and Knowledge Space Theory enable learner modeling at scale
Evidence quality hierarchy: RCT > external prediction > deployment > product features
Five critical gaps identified: source grounding + learner modeling integration, automatic pedagogical decisions, course boundary intelligence, obstacle detection, non-math subject validation
claims_requiring_review: Source-grounded responses prevent hallucination (feature exists but effectiveness not evaluated)
Learner modeling enables personalization (mechanisms exist but 'personalization' undefined)
Socratic questioning improves understanding (offered as option, not claimed as superior)
Learning OS works for any subject (evidence primarily from math)
recommendations_for_gate_2: Start with source grounding + file upload pattern (simpler than ALEKS knowledge structures)
Make pedagogical action selection explicit user choice (ChatGPT pattern)
Collect sparse evidence (observable behaviors, not inferred mastery)
Focus on single subject initially (consider FDS/Digital Logic for actual user need)
Avoid claiming learning effectiveness without pilot validation
